candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, Appendix A printed p.28 / PDF p.31, Health Promotion/Disease Prevention: educate clients on actions to promote and maintain health; assess/educate about health risks; preventive care and health maintenance recommendations
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — healthy hydration education
candidate.educational_objective: Teach that hydration needs are individualized and that total daily water intake includes water from beverages and foods, with needs increasing in settings such as heat or greater physical activity.

options.A: Water needs vary with factors such as activity and environment, and water from both beverages and foods contributes to total intake
options.B: Every healthy adult requires exactly the same fixed volume of plain water each day regardless of activity or climate
options.C: Water contained in foods does not contribute meaningfully to total daily water intake
options.D: Fluid intake should be reduced during hot weather or increased physical activity to prevent electrolyte imbalance

candidate.rationale: CDC states that daily water intake recommendations vary by factors including age, sex, pregnancy status, activity level, and breastfeeding status; the body needs more water in hot climates and with greater physical activity. Daily water comes from drinking water, other beverages, and water-containing foods. Therefore A is correct. B ignores individual variation, C excludes a verified source of water, and D reverses the expected effect of heat and activity on water needs.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Daily water needs vary by individual factors; needs increase with heat and physical activity; beverages and water-containing foods contribute to total daily water intake.
candidate.source_locator: Sections 'Your body needs more water when you are' and 'Meeting your water intake every day'
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
